evidence.claim: POST /api/notes/create creates an empty note owned by the caller with source_type='note' (INSERT-only, parameterized userId).
GET /api/notes/list returns only the requesting user's notes (WHERE d.user_id = ? AND d.source_type = 'note').

PATCH partially updates title/content, strips divider markup ('
---
' → '
'), and enforces the 50K content cap (413 when exceeded).
Defense-in-depth ordering present in every route: 401 if unauthenticated → 403 if hasNotesAccess false → owner+source_type row check via getNoteById before mutation.

The UPDATE carries user_id AND source_type='note' belt-and-braces guards in its WHERE; SET columns are a fixed whitelist (title/content/updated_at) with values parameterized — no user input interpolated into SQL.
owner + source_type guard on the target row uses parameterized id and userId.

Route test matrix evidences all acceptance dimensions: 401 unauth, 403 unflagged, 201 owner create, owner-scoped list, 404 non-owner PATCH, 413 over-cap, divider strip, and 404 on PATCH of a non-note (uploaded) doc confirming source_type guard. 10/10 pass.
DB spot-check after run shows additive-only effect: notes 2→3, uploaded docs 22 unchanged, questions 790 unchanged — no non-note rows modified, no cascade impact.
Scanner P0/P1A sacred-table-write and P1B raw_sql hits are confined to the pre-approved documents INSERT/UPDATE in queries.js; no migration, no DELETE, no middleware edit.
